plan.freeIntro: Free keeps the whole learning loop: starter and imported texts, phrase-aware lookups, saved vocabulary, practice, Anki sync, and portable data.
plan.libraryAllowance: Library allowance: {collections} collections, {lessons} lessons, and {words} journal words each month. Existing data is never deleted when a paid plan ends.
plan.fairUse: Generous fair-use safeguards apply to unusually large individual texts and bulk saved-data growth. They do not remove existing learner data or block exports.

byok.reverted: Reverted to your Readfox managed AI allowance
byok.heading: Bring your own AI key
byok.introFree: Free includes a small managed Gemini allowance. Add your own OpenRouter or Anthropic key to keep translating after that allowance and unlock richer AI actions without subscribing.
byok.introPaid: Use your own OpenRouter or Anthropic account for translations, explanations, journal corrections, and chat instead of the managed AI allowance.
byok.introTail: Your key is encrypted at rest and never shown again. BYOK does not enable managed voices; those remain a Cloud benefit.
byok.compareCloud: Prefer Readfox to handle both AI and higher-quality audio? <link>Compare Cloud plans</link>. Browser voices stay free either way.
byok.notConfigured: BYOK is not configured on this deployment yet.
byok.evalNote: Evaluated models are ordered by Afrikaans COMET score in Readfox's <link>reproducible translation eval</link>. Gaps below roughly 1.5 points are statistical ties; Flash Lite is the unevaluated low-cost default.
byok.validates: Readfox validates the key with {provider} before saving it. Provider errors never include your key.
byok.protectedTitle: How your API key is protected
byok.protectedEncryption: Keys are encrypted before they reach the database using AES-256-GCM with a fresh random nonce. Authentication data binds each ciphertext to your account and chosen provider, so an encrypted row cannot be moved to another account.
byok.protectedStorage: The deployment encryption key is held separately in AWS Parameter Store. Your API key is write-only: Readfox never sends it back to the browser, includes it in exports, or logs upstream credential details.
byok.protectedOpenSource: Readfox is open source, so you can verify how credentials are encrypted, stored, and selected at request time. <link>Inspect the implementation</link>.

llm.noModels: No models reported by this endpoint — type the model name instead.
llm.heading: AI Provider
llm.intro: Choose how translations are powered. Anthropic uses cloud AI for the highest quality. Local & self-hosted covers any OpenAI-compatible server — Ollama, LM Studio, Apfel, vLLM, and friends — with one endpoint, an optional API key, and a model name.
llm.bothConfigured: Both credentials are configured. Choose which to use — connection will be tested automatically.
llm.oauthHelp: Uses your Claude Pro or Team subscription credits. Run claude setup-token to obtain a token. Note: slower initial startup than API keys.
llm.presetHelp: A shortcut that fills in the endpoint below. You can edit it afterwards.
llm.endpointHelp: Base URL of your server — the app appends /v1. It's called server-side, so localhost works even when lector is hosted elsewhere.
llm.apiKeyPlaceholder: leave empty for local servers without auth
llm.apiKeyHelp: Sent as a Bearer token from the server (never exposed to the browser after save). Only needed for reverse-proxied, cloud, or otherwise authenticated endpoints.
llm.modelPlaceholder: Type a model name, or fetch the list
llm.modelHelp: Pick from the fetched list (servers like LM Studio & Ollama report it via /v1/models) or just type any model name your server accepts.

anki.addonIntro: The add-on syncs from inside Anki itself, so it works no matter where this Lector runs: words you queue become cards the next time Anki opens, and your review results flow back automatically.
anki.addonStep1: Create an API token in API Tokens below, scoped to anki.
anki.addonStep2: Install the add-on from <link>anki-addon in the Lector repository</link> (Anki Desktop 2.1.50+).
anki.addonStep3: In Anki, open Tools → Add-ons → Lector Sync → Config and set api_url to the address below and api_token to your token.
anki.addonMobile: AnkiDroid and AnkiMobile can't run add-ons — sync on desktop and AnkiWeb carries the results to your devices.
anki.connectFailed: Failed to connect to Anki. Make sure Anki is running with AnkiConnect installed.
anki.heading: Anki Integration
anki.connectionHelp: AnkiConnect reaches Anki on this computer from the browser. The add-on syncs from inside Anki instead — use it when Lector is served over HTTPS or runs on another machine.
anki.urlHint: Hint: Use Tailscale IP for remote Anki (e.g., http://100.x.x.x:8765)
anki.vocabDeckHelp: Deck for basic cards from reader vocabulary
anki.clozeDeckHelp: Deck for cloze cards from practice mode
anki.cardTypeHelp: Basic shows front/back, Cloze creates fill-in-the-blank cards
anki.comingSoonBody: Anki sync is coming. Words you save will become Anki cards, and your reviews will sync back. Until then, review your saved words on the Practice page.

twoFactor.heading: Two-Factor Authentication
twoFactor.intro: Protect your account with one-time codes from an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, 1Password, Authy, …) on top of your password.
twoFactor.statusOn: Two-factor authentication is on. Signing in asks for a code from your authenticator app.
twoFactor.step1: 1. Scan this QR code with your authenticator app
twoFactor.cantScan: Can’t scan? Enter this key manually:
twoFactor.step2: 2. Enter the 6-digit code the app shows now
twoFactor.saveCodes: Save these backup codes somewhere safe — each one signs you in once if you lose your authenticator, and they won’t be shown again.

apiTokens.heading: API Tokens
apiTokens.intro: Create personal access tokens for CLI or API access. Tokens are scoped to specific permissions.
apiTokens.copyNow: Copy this token now — it won't be shown again.
apiTokens.revokeConfirm: Revoke token "{name}"? This cannot be undone.
apiTokens.empty: No tokens created yet. Generate one to use the CLI or access the API remotely.

deleteAccount.startFailed: Could not start account deletion. Please try again.
deleteAccount.heading: Delete account
deleteAccount.intro: Permanently delete your account and all of your data — books, vocabulary, cloze progress, journal entries, chat history, and settings. This cannot be undone, and is separate from exporting a backup above.
deleteAccount.billingWarning: If you have a paid subscription, cancel it first: deleting your account here does not cancel billing (payments are handled by Paddle, our merchant of record — the manage-subscription link is in your Paddle receipt emails).
deleteAccount.sent: Check your email and open the link we just sent in this browser to permanently delete your account. The link expires in 24 hours.
